channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: NYC's Mamdani condemns Tuberville's anti-Muslim posts as "bigotry"
item.description: Speaking at a public iftar dinner, held to break the daily Ramadan fast, New York City Mayor Mamdani described Sen. Tuberville's anti-Muslim rhetoric as "bigotry" and "hatred."

item.title: A record number of political parties register for Haiti's first election in a decade
item.description: A record 280 political parties had registered by Thursday's deadline to participate in Haiti's first general election in a decade, hopeful for a chance to help ease their country's multiple crises.

item.title: Cuba will release 51 people from prison in an unexpected move
item.description: The announcement was made just hours before Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel is scheduled to speak early Friday "to address national and international issues."

item.title: Senate passes bipartisan housing bill targeting large investors and easing regulations
item.description: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act would ban large investors from buying up single-family homes.

item.title: Benicio del Toro reflects on the acting class that changed his life
item.description: One of del Toro's early acting teachers taught him to understand his character before learning lines. He's up for an Oscar for his role in One Battle After Another. Originally broadcast June 12, 2025.

item.title: Egg prices have taken a beating. What's behind the drop?
item.description: A year ago, eggs were scarce and prices were sky-high. But avian flu took a much smaller toll on America's egg-laying chickens this winter than last, and egg prices have tumbled 42%.

item.title: Bucking stigma, more places turn to factory-built for affordable housing
item.description: Mobile homes have long been zoned out of cities and suburbs. But with updated designs and a housing shortage, they're increasingly being welcomed as more-affordable starter homes.

item.title: Democrats set a turnout record in Texas, so is this the year it turns blue?
item.description: Latinos helped Texas Democrats set the new record for a primary, but the state has been a white whale for the party for decades.

item.title: Medicaid can share data with ICE. Here's how that 180-degree change spreads fear
item.description: When Medicaid began sharing personal data with federal immigration authorities last year, it upended decades of explicit promises to patients. Now, even eligible immigrants fear getting the health coverage.

item.title: Trump wants more apprenticeships. An Arkansas manufacturer is giving it a try
item.description: President Trump has touted apprenticeships as part of his promise of a golden era for American workers. But are his administration's investments enough?
